overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via reply-all emails outside a posted meeting, declined to find an intentional violation, and ordered compliance and public release of the emails.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting via email about covering a playground display after a religious-speech complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board’s emails regarding this matter constituted impermissible deliberation outside of a posted meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the Board's email deliberation was an intentional violation of the Open Meeting Law under G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c).
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find an intentional violation.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release the July 23 chain of emails, including the deliberative emails, within 30 days of receipt of the determination if not already done.
Caution that a future similar violation determination may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
